we have identified a genome-wide linkage peak on chromosome 3, and that the location and strength of this peak are consistent with a recent report from another group of researchers.
we have replicated the finding of linkage of extreme human longevity to 3q22.3 and have identified possible additional loci on chromosomes 8q23 and 17q23.
we have replicated linkage of extreme longevity to 3 p22-24 in humans and identified other possible loci.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of human longevity.
the identification of the genetic factors responsible for human longevity, which is a complex trait that is determined by multiple genes, as well as by environmental factors and their interactions.
identifying the molecular genetic basis of human longevity, and the present study represents a step toward this goal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3p24 locus is a major locus for human longevity.
the linkage of longevity on chromosome 3 has been confirmed and the region narrowed to a 3 Mb region, and that the linkage on chromosome 18 has also been confirmed, and narrowed to a 2 Mb region.
the evidence for a role of 3p24 in human longevity is strong.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the linkage of 3p24 to exceptional longevity in our study and in the HMS study is a strong replication.

we have identified a region of chromosome 3 that is strongly linked to exceptional human longevity, that the linkage is robust to the inclusion of a larger sample of unrelated individuals (the HMS sample), and that the linkage is not limited to a single population.
the linkage of 3p24-22 to extreme longevity in humans is now well established.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of extreme longevity in humans is a promising approach to the study of the genetics of human aging and lifespan.
it is possible, with a sufficiently large sample size, to detect linkage in human longevity.
the search for longevity genes in humans is not futile.
